line: Park Jong-gi, assistant manager, IT Sales. Four years in the job, and always the nice one.

All morning his team leader's voice follows him down the street: the price, the delays at the Guangzhou plant, and the night a restaurant gave the team extra meat and Park made everyone pay for it. Whose side is he on?
His wife calls: she has enrolled their son in an academy. He calls the supplier about the late shipment, hears that the man's daughter is having a hard time, and tells him not to worry about it.
He eats a bun and a carton of milk standing on a strip of grass by the crossing. Then his heart starts pounding, and he brings it all back up.
That night he drinks alone at a street stall and calls an old friend who quit his job and started again.
His friend, on the phone: you can't make everyone happy. Choose, and take responsibility for the choice.

In the alley by his front gate he sits down and doesn't go in. He's happy: a wife, a son, a home, all resting on a job he's afraid of. That's the trouble. He doesn't have the nerve to carry this much happiness.
The next morning, on the roof. Thirteen days to the interns' PT, not that Park knows or cares. An envelope in his hand: RESIGNATION LETTER.
An intern comes out onto the roof rehearsing a presentation under his breath, waving one arm.
Park slips the envelope into his jacket.
Mr. Park from IT Sales? I'm Jang Geu-rae, an intern. Mr. Oh says you're an exemplary salesman, the kind who builds relationships with compassion.
beats.speaker: jg

line: That was all Oh said. But Park's eyes are shining, so Jang adds a little more.
Sales is a war of nerves. Let the other side see you're soft, and they'll walk all over you.
beats.speaker: ms_parkjg

line: A supplier missed a deadline once. Their director came to beg. I told him: we'll hold you to the terms of the contract.
beats.speaker: ms_parkjg

line: It never happened. But saying it, he feels lighter.
Come with me to one of our suppliers. They've caused a little trouble today. I'll square it with Mr. Oh.
beats.speaker: ms_parkjg

line: Back in Sales 3, Oh hears where Jang has gone. Park from IT Sales, suddenly so friendly? A bit much, he thinks.
The supplier deals with a Chinese semiconductor firm. Lately its shipments to One International keep slipping.
I'm not here to accuse anyone. It's a relationship of trust. A visit just keeps them on their toes.
beats.speaker: ms_parkjg

line: In the corridor, voices behind a half-open door: the new client comes first; hold One International off by phone. Park is soft. Give him an excuse.
Mr. Kwon comes out whistling, sees them, and freezes.
Mr. Park! You should have called first. We've just been diversifying a little...
beats.speaker: kw

line: So this is how they see him. Easy. And Jang is watching him with shining eyes, waiting to see the man from the story on the roof.
Mr. Kwon. Can we hold to... the terms of the contract?
beats.speaker: ms_parkjg

line: If he doesn't change now, he never will.
The president is calm. Ten years they've done business together, he says. Problems on both sides, always settled like friends.
So when you say the contract, Mr. Park: do you mean ending it, or compensation?
beats.speaker: ceo

line: I... I'll have to ask head office.
beats.speaker: ms_parkjg

line: Then the president turns on his own men: how could they betray their oldest partner for a few more won? He'll go to One International himself and beg.
Park is shaking. Ten years, ended because of him, when all he had to do was look the other way. He opens his mouth to back down.
Jang reads the room like a board. The rage is for his staff, but it's aimed at Park. A clever trick only proves the game has been going badly for the one who plays it.
Under the table, Jang texts Kim Dong-sik: call me, please. The phone rings.
We've stayed too long. You'll get told off. Maybe we should have called first...
beats.speaker: ms_parkjg

line: Why would I get told off? We're here on business. And I'm with you.
beats.speaker: ms_jang

line: Jang steps into the doorway and answers loudly: yes, Mr. Kim, the president says he'll come to One International himself to explain. Yes, he said so himself.
No trick of his own. He takes the president at his word, out loud, where it can't be taken back.
Meeting Room 3. Director Choi of IT, the department head, and the risk, evaluation and legal teams. The supplier's president waits in another room.
Evaluation: small losses. Risk: low. Legal: this is the seventh late shipment, so the contract must be looked at again.
How did it come to this?
beats.speaker: dir

line: Park stands up. The room is airless, and he's still worrying about the supplier. Jang scribbles on a sheet of paper and slides it over as if it were a reference document.
BE IRRESPONSIBLE! In baduk you have to know when to abandon stones in danger. You can't save everyone. Save yourself first.
Park explains: seven delays, a new Chinese client, a supplier putting first orders first. The executives nod: without his visit they'd never have known.
But I never took the measures I should have. I didn't see how serious it was. The one who's been deceiving everyone... was me.
beats.speaker: ms_parkjg

line: Every face around the table becomes his own. Shipping costs went up with oil, he says, and One International still cut what it paid, and he never argued for them. Hold him responsible, not them.
How long have you been with us?
beats.speaker: dir

line: You're a sentimental man. Nobody drops a ten-year partner over this. Bring me their president.
beats.speaker: dir

line: Afterwards Jang sits with his head down. He has never felt so wretched, not even after losing a game.
Everyone plays their own game of baduk. And he tried to play Park's for him.
Thank you, Mr. Jang. You took off the skin that was holding me in. Thank you.
beats.speaker: ms_parkjg

line: Park takes the envelope out of his jacket and feeds it to the shredder.
That evening he calls his wife. Their son won't go to the academy after all. Let the boy have time to think.
You can't play another man's game for him. In twelve days Jang will have to play his own.
Twelve days to the PT. The supplier signs a new contract: three per cent off for two years. Park isn't punished. He writes a report on what went wrong.
Risk is part of trade. There's no end to hunting for a scapegoat, so the company hunts for improvements. You still write that report carefully, mind.
beats.speaker: kd

line: Now go and help Sun Ji-young with her buyer meeting, both of you. Learn from her.
beats.speaker: kd

line: Sun Ji-young, deputy head of Sales Team 1: wiry, fast and exact. Hard subcontractors turn helpful after one meeting with her.
She is on the phone to her husband: she can't get to the daycare by seven; he was supposed to fetch their daughter by six.
Fewer words, more pictures. Times New Roman, fourteen point, black. No hyperlinks. Show me the layout before you place a single image.
beats.speaker: sun

line: Should I add the delivery figures?
beats.speaker: ms_jang

line: Ask Mr. Han. You picked him as your partner over everyone in the intake. I hold grudges.
beats.speaker: ahn

line: The meeting goes well. Then Sun's phone again: her husband can't come, the teacher has to go home.
It's personal. You two did very well today. You can go.
beats.speaker: sun

line: She won't ask a junior for a personal favour. But the next call ends with: it'll be midnight before I can get there.
Ma'am, I live out that way.
beats.speaker: ms_jang

line: In the taxi, Ahn says it plainly: men never see what it costs a woman to become a deputy head.
The doorbell rings. Every child left in the all-day class comes to the door to see whose mother it is. Then they go back to their blocks.
Jang asks if they can take the children out to the playground. Someone has to supervise. The young teacher, Ms. Ha, says she'll stay.
Ahn pushes the swings. Jang carries a boy on his shoulders. One by one the mothers come, all of them running.
Are you two a couple? It feels like you like her.
beats.speaker: ha

line: She's a coworker I can rely on.
beats.speaker: ms_jang

line: Sun comes long after dark. Somi is asleep on the bench next to Jang.
Thursday, lunch. My treat. Promises like this are easy to forget, so I'm fixing it now. And come in at eight tomorrow.
beats.speaker: sun

line: Late at night. Through the kitchen door, her husband is washing up. Somi is asleep. In Somi's bag there's a crayon drawing.
Mummy, in her office suit, seen from behind: walking away, a phone at her ear.
This is me. She's drawn me from behind.
beats.speaker: ms_sun

line: They work this hard for the three of them, and they're hurting themselves doing it. Things will be easier when Somi's older, he says. He has golf tomorrow.
Before office hours, a client is already on the phone. Sun rings the bell and keeps talking. Ms. Ha takes Somi in. Sun turns to go.
Somi stands behind the glass door, watching her mother walk away.
That's the drawing. Not her face. Her back, walking away. It's what Somi sees every morning.
Sun tells the client she'll call back. She comes back, kneels and bows to her daughter, and Somi giggles. She holds her.
She won't put her daughter off for the sake of making a living.
Jang is in at eight, as Sun told them. Sun is late, and comes in looking lighter.
On Thursday she takes them to lunch, as promised, and shows them a new drawing from Somi. This time Mummy has a face.
Back at his desk the phone rings: Ms. Ha, from the daycare, asking if he'd like a drink some time.
Ten days to the PT. The pair topic is free. The individual topic comes the day before.
The intern in glasses from the study group, Jang Baek-gi, top school and top marks, asks what they're all thinking.
Fifteen of us. They'll take half, surely?
beats.speaker: bk

line: Last time they started with thirty. Two got in.
beats.speaker: ahn

line: Somewhere on the floor a senior bellows at somebody: the calculator does the sums, so how did you get them wrong?
Then Han is back from the Ulsan plant and bursts into the reference room: Geu-rae! Great, great! Champagne when the results come out.
Culture and trade. Nice idea, boring title. It's not what we sell. It's who we sell to, and why they need it.
beats.speaker: han

line: Jang's proposal had one phrase in it: limited by culture. Han builds the whole pitch on it.

A woman in a hot, humid country: does she give up make-up, or want make-up that won't melt? And polypropylene fibre: light, warm, dries fast, but it won't take dye, so nobody uses it. As thermal underwear for long winters, who cares about the colour?
beats.speaker: han

line: How do you know all this?
beats.speaker: ms_jang

line: Is this what fieldwork at the Ulsan plant does to a person?
Nine days to the PT. Ahn's partner, Lee Sang-hyun, is at his old university making a video with the broadcasting club.
It's a team project. Respect my opinion too. ...Honestly, I've been teamed up with a bomb.
Who are you calling a bomb?
beats.speaker: ms_ahn

line: Baek-gi and his partner pool their research and find it's identical, down to the same typo. They both paid for the same website.
Some customs people embrace, and some feel like a cage. There has to be a point in between that satisfies both.
beats.speaker: ms_jang

line: That's it. The intersection. They don't want an answer from two-month interns. They know more than we do. What matters is the question.
beats.speaker: han

line: Isn't a business that satisfies that person a business that satisfies everyone? We end the PT on that question, and we put it to the man who decides: the president.
beats.speaker: han

line: Han thinks like a fast baduk player. Every time Jang says he'll read up on something, Han has already named the book and dismissed it.
None. No films, no dramas either. And don't laugh. I like working best.
beats.speaker: han

line: That's the secret of his speed. Why would Jang laugh?
That evening, waiting outside the tower, Jang goes back over the day.
A week to the PT, and the interns still have their day jobs. Han is sent to the copier again and stands there shaking with fury.
Kim's advice to Jang: text on the slides is safer than pictures; the judges sit through a dozen PTs, and words give them a map. Oh's: say the script out loud. Nerves make you fast.
Sun said fewer words and more pictures; Kim says words. Each is right for their own audience, and the judges are Kim's.
That's Mr. Kim's opinion. I don't call anyone boss who doesn't know what goes on in the field.
beats.speaker: han

line: Your boss? We're both interns, punk.
beats.speaker: han

line: A fist, a grab, a scuffle. Then a truce of sorts. Do your job in the PT, Han tells him, and don't get in my way.

The files go in on a CD. Then the stopwatch: Han runs fourteen minutes, then seventeen, and his hands shake on the script. The limit is ten, and five for questions. He has memorised every sentence, and they shout at each other over which ones to cut.
Look who's talking. Let's go, nuclear bomb.
beats.speaker: ahn

line: Eight o'clock at night. Every intern is hanging about outside the tower. Their phones all go off at once.
From Human Resources: what would you sell to your team-project partner, and why?
They have to sell something to the last person they'd want to sell to.
Whatever you sell, your partner's answer will show how you judged him. The other person will tell you who you are.
Some interns live in the catalogue room. Some trawl the internet. Lee rings a friend who sells insurance.
A pen? Everything made in the field ends up on paper in the office. But a pen won't persuade Han.
Oh is in the lobby, on his way out to a factory.
Is the field as important as the office?
beats.speaker: ms_jang

line: Important in different ways. If only the field mattered, why would we need a building this size? Everything made in the field is finished in the office. You run till your feet burn out there, and you sweat your feet in here.
beats.speaker: oh

line: Sweat your feet in here. Jang thanks him and runs back inside.
PT day. The interns file in carrying boxes. Oh's slippers are poking out of Jang's. Han sees them and mutters: is he out of his mind?

Executives in the front row, department heads behind, Oh among them. One executive smiles at the company video; Jang guesses he's remembering a mine contract and his years in the field. He hopes Han gets a middle age with moments like that.
Ten minutes to present, five for questions, nothing that wasn't submitted, and the clock starts when your names are called.
The first pair, Jang Ki-seok and Ku Hyun-woo, flap up the aisle in onesies and swimming flippers: they're the Jang-Ku Team, here to leave their footprints on the world.
Next! Come back in proper clothes. We're not here to play.
beats.speaker: ex

line: Ahn and Lee: Avatar, global companies stripping the resources of poor countries, and an alternative. Ahn presents alone and never once looks at the screen.
Mr. Lee hasn't said a word. Ms. Ahn, why didn't you warn your partner?
beats.speaker: ex

line: Because we're being interviewed for the job.
beats.speaker: ahn

line: The Jang-Ku Team come back in suits. A judge spots the company logo on their slide, screen-captured off the website.
Nobody in the room is laughing now.
Not yet. What does an office worker wear into battle?
beats.speaker: ms_jang

line: One presenter forgets his lines and asks to start again. One mixes up risks and crises. One admits he chose this company because he didn't think he'd get in anywhere better.
Are you asking us to hire you or not?
beats.speaker: ms_examiner

line: One team has a flashy show and is told it belongs at an advertising firm. One runs out of time. One quotes 2010 figures, when the company has its own research institute.
Only Ahn hasn't lost the war of nerves. The judges mutter that they may hire a record low. How many last year? Two. Then one?
Next: Jang Geu-rae and Han Seok-yul. Han has always been the confident one. He swallows, and swallows again.
In his team's office the phones keep ringing for him. On his desk his mobile buzzes: a text from Mum. Did you take your anxiety medicine?
Our topic is a proposal for people limited by culture. Culture is defined as...
beats.speaker: ms_han

line: He's reading it off the page, breathing hard.
Is something chasing you? Catch your breath.
beats.speaker: ex

line: May I take my medicine, sir? It's a drink. I'll be quick.
beats.speaker: ms_han

line: He gulps it, and sprays it out coughing. He can't speak.
My partner choked on his drink. I'll continue.
beats.speaker: jg

line: His old baduk teacher's voice: there's no such thing as a stone played for no reason. Chance is a gift to those already prepared. So shall we get ready?
Jang knows the material. He has never presented. He stammers.
It's hard to listen to. No business vocabulary. Have you ever been out in the field? To a factory? You've never left the office, have you?
beats.speaker: ex

line: Han hears Jang's "No, sir", plain and unashamed, and remembers.

A small boy tells his father his fingernails are dirty. Grease, the father says. It won't come off. Are you ashamed? Then a strike, and everyone who joined it is fired, and a boy in the street jeers at the factory man with no job.
Han tips his head back. His lip trembles. Yes. The field is the best.
Well done, Mr. Jang. I'm sorry for the trouble. I'll pick up where he left off.
beats.speaker: ms_han

line: Dad. I'm not ashamed of you. Or of the field.
Now Han speaks the language of the field: full-container loads, the forwarder, the plant. The executive who once worked a mine is smiling.
It's never been traded from Korea, so your costing's an estimate. Did you get it right? Too much for you?
beats.speaker: ex

line: Too much, sir? I'll work it out now.
beats.speaker: han

line: He has Jang read him the numbers. The exchange rate? Look it up yourself, sir, he says. I'm past that. The estimate is right.
And freight? Didn't it go up with oil?
beats.speaker: ex

line: Han hesitates. A voice from the interns' seats:
No, sir. Air freight rose sixteen point six per cent. Sea and land didn't. And on a CNF contract the exporter pays cost and freight.
beats.speaker: ahn

line: Don't tell me you're the president's daughter. Or staff pretending to be an intern.
beats.speaker: ex

line: Did she help them, or herself? Would she ever do that for Jang? What are they to her?
He wrote the text and found the papers. Speaking isn't writing. If you don't hold the room, the words go thin. That's his limit, for now. I'd like him to stay.
beats.speaker: oh

line: I hope he doesn't fall for the question tomorrow. It's a paradox.
beats.speaker: sun

line: The next day. Each intern sells to their partner, the partner says whether they'll buy and why, and the questions come from the seniors of each intern's own team.
Wallets, a belt, a brag about shoes. Baek-gi sells his partner a hand mirror: learn to manage your face before you do business. The partner, red to the ears, buys it.
Ahn plays it safe and doesn't stand out, because she doesn't need to. A judge writes: a textbook.

Synthetic textiles from our Ulsan plant. Nylon, polyester, acrylic, polypropylene. And with them, this notebook: the losses, the miscommunication, the conditions on the line. I'm selling Mr. Jang the voice of the field.
beats.speaker: han

line: I'll buy the notebook. Not the textiles.
beats.speaker: ms_jang

line: Because I want to sell them with Mr. Han. I'll study these notes so I'm not a burden to him. Can we sell them together?
beats.speaker: ms_jang

line: I'll answer when I've seen what you're selling me.
beats.speaker: han

line: My boss's dress shoes. Clean, because office workers rarely go out, but must look right when they do. And these, the same man's slippers, the spikes worn down to the shape of his foot. The office is a field too. I'm selling you the combat boots of the office.
beats.speaker: ms_jang

line: In the second row, Oh looks down at his socks. So that's where they went.
I won't buy them. Call the office the field? A few sheets of office paper can get a whole line fired. Real combat boots have steel toes, so a dropped tool doesn't break your foot.
beats.speaker: han

line: The packed train in. Ten departments to agree one number. A lawyer over a single line of a contract. All night, waiting for a buyer abroad to say yes. What the factory makes starts as a row of decisions.
beats.speaker: ms_jang

line: His teacher: there is no meaningless stone on the board. A stone in a dead group means a misreading; leave it to die, and use it to win.
No product this company makes exists for no reason. A failed one means a bad estimate. You learn from it. I don't think my field is so different from yours.
beats.speaker: ms_jang

line: Han looks at the slippers for a long moment. He steps out of his own shoes and into them.
I'll... buy these slippers. And let's sell those together.
beats.speaker: han

line: That's the end of the PT. Results by email and text, in a week.
Back upstairs, the interns clear their desks into boxes.
You did well. Not all of you will get in. But I hope to see you again.
beats.speaker: oh

line: In the lobby on the way out, Jang tells Ahn she was amazing. She shrugs: she's done this a few times before.
That night Han carries two bags into an empty office and drops a new pair of slippers under every desk.
For a week he sleeps, and doesn't touch the computer. He replays Cho Chikun's game, the one he played in a wheelchair, so he can accept whatever comes.
A week later he logs in. All over Seoul, phones chime.
Baek-gi, on a mountain top: hired. A safe bet. Ahn, in a department store: hired. Han, in his rented room: hired.
Intern Jang Geu-rae. Hired as a contract worker for two years.
The others are permanent staff. He has two years. The parachute is in, but only on a lease.
Mum. I... I think I got a job. Thank you.
beats.speaker: ms_jang

line: The first day. Han at the door: not bad. A fist bump. Then Ahn and Baek-gi, who of course got in.
The president reads Ahn's file: two companies already, an executive track she walked away from because it was too easy. To Jang he says nothing at all.
For the next two years Jang belongs to the team whose leader asked for him: Sales Team 3, the Storm Troops.
Tradition, says Oh: the new hires choose their first work suits at a department store. The prices are four, six hundred thousand won. Card or cash? They panic. Oh and Kim are behind a rail, laughing.
A suit? On what you earn? Here. Our gift to new people.
beats.speaker: oh

line: Black ties for the men. A black scarf for Ahn.
Put them on now. We have somewhere to go.
beats.speaker: oh

line: Past the subway exit, along a stone wall, banners: give back the jobs of the wrongly fired.
A tarpaulin tent on the pavement. A portrait with a black ribbon, rows of names, candles, flowers. Workers laid off from a car plant, and the ones who didn't live to see it end.
Before you start working for a living, come and see the people who lost theirs. Go on. Pay your respects.
beats.speaker: ms_oh

line: They bow, in their black ties. Han bows longest.
To live by your work is to endure, whatever comes. It's the road toward a life that's complete.
Ahn takes his photo. Behind him, an office tower. In front of him, the first day of two years.
